Q3 Long Question Time Complexity in Algorithm Analysis Time complexity is a way to measure how the running time of an algorithm increases as the input size increases. It helps us understand how efficient an algorithm is. Instead of measuring actual time in seconds, we focus on the number of basic operations an algorithm performs. Big O Notation: Big O notation is used to describe the worst-case time complexity of an algorithm. It shows how performance grows with input size. Common Examples: O(1) — Constant Time: Accessing an element in an array, e.g. arr[i] O(log n) — Logarithmic Time: Binary Search — each step divides the problem in half. O(n) — Linear Time: Linear Search — each element is checked once. O(n²) — Quadratic Time: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort — nested loops over data.

Q3 Long Question Common Clauses in Terms of Use and Their Protection Privacy and Data Use — protects user information and explains data collection. User Obligations — sets out users' rules/responsibilities and prevents misuse. Limitation of Liability — protects service providers from full blame for issues. Termination of Service — allows account suspension if rules are broken. Dispute Resolution — helps resolve conflicts between provider and users fairly. Protection: these clauses protect service providers by reducing risk and protecting the service, and protect users by explaining their rights, privacy, safety, and fair-use rules.
